about: Every change to Flood-Net's agent API (https://floodwarning.net/api/v1 and https://floodwarning.net/api/mcp) that someone using it would notice — a route, a field, a limit, a tool — newest first. Each entry is emailed once to everyone on the API notify list (sign up at https://floodwarning.net/api#notify). Served as JSON at https://floodwarning.net/api/v1/changelog and written up in docs/agent-api.md, under Changes. Add an entry in the same push as the change: it is what tells people.

entries.title: Silent stations are said as not heard by Flood-Net, and point to ARRO
entries.summary: A station Flood-Net calls silent is one its own receivers have not heard — not one that has stopped reporting. The stations report to the Bureau through its own base stations, and Flood-Net often hears a station one way where the Bureau has several: on 3 November eight Gold Coast stations behind Tallai were silent here overnight and complete in the Bureau's ARRO. So the words now say what is known. The findings' titles read "Not heard — missed its last N checks", "Not heard for 15 h", "Not heard for 15 h, then heard again" and "N stations behind X went unheard together" (they read "Silent —", "Quiet for", "Went silent … then came back" and "went quiet together"); details say Flood-Net heard nothing; and each silence's action starts by looking in ARRO, where the station's arro_site (GET /api/v1/stations/{id}) names its site. GET /api/v1/health/silent and get_silent_stations say the same in their notes and descriptions. The route, the tool, the kinds (silent, silent-spell, repeater-down, area-silence, shared-spell) and every field are as they were — match on kind, not on a title's words. Findings already open take the new words at the server's next run, within fifteen minutes.

entries.title: One ALERT burst heard several ways is one reading
entries.summary: A legacy ALERT frame carries no time of its own, so each receiver stamps it when it heard it. When one burst arrived several ways — direct, through a repeater, through an ALERT2 concentrator — the copies were a second or so apart and were stored as separate readings: about 6% of ALERT readings were a copy of another. From today, a reading on an ALERT address with the same value as one stored within 8 seconds either side is that reading heard again: it is counted in dup_count instead of being a row of its own. So the raw readings of a legacy ALERT station (GET /api/v1/stations/{id}/readings) have fewer near-identical rows and more dup_count; ALERT2 self-reports and satellite or cellular stations, which carry the station's own time, are as they were. Readings stored before today keep their twins. No field, route or limit has changed.

entries.title: A station's radio path to base, with the fade margins Flood-Net saved
entries.summary: New: GET /api/v1/stations/{id}/radio-path (MCP tool get_radio_path) follows a station's readings to a base station. It lists the repeaters whose pass ranges carry the station's ALERT addresses (the nearest 5 within 150 km), each one's routes on along the backbone to a base station (100 km a hop, at most 4 repeaters — the Stations map's own rules), and every hop's fade margin as Flood-Net saved it: both ways, its band against the saved thresholds, frequency, distance, line of sight, model and date, and whether it is stale, with the reasons in words. It names the best path and its weakest hop, says plainly where a hop has not been modelled, and gives the station's attenuator tests from site visits. Please note: every saved figure is stale today — worked out in September 2026 with an older model that reads much too low — and each answer says so. The station dossier gains a radio_path section and its links a radio_path link. Nothing that was there before has changed.

entries.title: This list of changes, and an email when the API changes
entries.summary: New: GET /api/v1/changelog lists every change to the API that someone using it would notice — routes, fields, limits, tools — newest first, and the API's index (GET /api/v1/) links to it as changelog. To be told by email, put your address in the form at https://floodwarning.net/api#notify: you are sent a link to confirm it, nothing else until you do, and every email after that has a link to stop them. Nothing about the station data has changed.

entries.title: The ACMA licences at a station's site, or at a point
entries.summary: New: GET /api/v1/stations/{id}/acma (MCP tool get_acma_licences) gives the ACMA licence numbers Flood-Net records for a station, each looked up in the ACMA's Register of Radiocommunications Licences, and the register's licences at sites within radius_m of it (500 m by default, 5 km at most) — licensee, frequencies, power, emission, authorised date, distance, the site's stated precision, and whether each is on the station's channel — with the repeaters that relay a field station. GET /api/v1/acma?near=lat,lon (MCP tool acma_licences_near) does the same for a point, for a site not built yet. The station dossier gains an acma section and its links an acma link. The register is a weekly extract; every answer gives its date. Nothing that was there before has changed.
